title: Sarasota County School District Referendum: Renewal of the One-Mill Levy
what_it_does: School-district ballot question (Yes / No). Passes with a simple majority of votes cast on the question.
ballot_summary: Continues Funding for Teachers, Workforce Training, Student Achievement Through Renewal of Ad Valorem Millage Referendum. Shall the Sarasota County School District continue the 1 mill per year ad valorem millage to retain and recruit quality teachers; provide workforce training; improve school safety and security; preserve the arts; upgrade technology and classroom resources; fund other education programs and school operational needs; beginning July 1, 2026 and ending June 30, 2030; and sharing funds with charter schools proportionate with student enrollment, with oversight of all funds by an independent committee of citizens?
what_yes_means: A YES vote continues the one-mill school levy, in place since 2002, for 2026 through 2030; the district estimates about $114 million a year.
what_no_means: A NO vote lets the levy expire, removing that funding for teacher pay, workforce training, arts, security and technology.
verified_ballot_note: Ballot language from the Better Schools for Sarasota County committee's posting of the resolution (https://yesforsarasotacountyschools.com/ballot-language/); the School Board placed the renewal on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. Confirm on the Sarasota sample ballot.
